How the route works now (server/routes/report-os.ts, GET /runs/:id/rendered, about lines 1875-1891):

- On 'not-verifiable' it falls through to the ordinary re-render, which carries no `sealed` flag.

Why 'intact' always means the served document was checked against the seal (verifyStoredSeal):
- 'intact' requires the audit-chain check to pass: exactly one 'report_os.run_finalized' row, `payload_hash = sha256(new_values::text)`, and a seal hash present.
- It also requires `s.ok && d.ok`. `d.ok` means the served document, re-hashed under the canonicalizer the chain row recorded, equals the chain row's sealHash, and its provenance-atom count matches.
- 'not-verifiable' is only reachable when no sealed document is stored. So no stored document can be served under that verdict, and the route's `stored.document` guard holds.
- The served object is the same reference that was hashed. The canonicalizer (stableStringify, or the frozen v1) covers every key a JSON round-trip can produce, so no part of the response sits outside the hash.
- The payload binding holds on a real database: audit_logs.new_values is a `json` column (text kept as written), and hashPayload is sha256 of JSON.stringify of that same value.

findings.title: An unchained 'report_os.run_finalized' row written by the app role is accepted as the record of the act, so a forged document reads as 'intact' and GET /rendered serves it with sealed:true
findings.evidence: readChainRecords (line 206-208) selects only `new_values::text, payload_hash, occurred_at`. It never reads sha256_chain, hmac_seal or chain_seq. The only binding it checks is payload_hash = sha256(new_values::text), and anyone who writes the row can compute that. The INSERT trigger audit_logs_chain_position returns NEW unchanged when `NEW.sha256_chain IS NULL` (it treats the row as legacy). The integrity report reads only `WHERE sha256_chain IS NOT NULL` (server/services/audit/chain.ts:650), so it never sees such a row. Also, verifyStoredSeal never requires the electronic_signatures row that finalize always writes in the same transaction. Probe on the local CI-shaped database concept2cure-ri_dbtest, inside one transaction that was rolled back afterwards (scratchpad/probe-forge.ts). As `app_service` (is_superuser off, app.rls_enforce=on), on a run that was never finalized: (1) UPDATE report_runs SET status='final'; (2) UPDATE report_snapshots with {seal, sealedDocument:<forged doc 'FORGED: ready to file.'>}; (3) INSERT one audit_logs row: action report_os.run_finalized, documentStored:true, payload_hash=sha256(nv), sha256_chain NULL. readRunSeal returned verdict 'intact' with signature null, and all three checks ok. The audit-chain detail read: "the chain link itself is verified by the audit-trail integrity report". The row read back as {sha256_chain:null, hmac_seal:null, chain_seq:null}. readVerifiedSealedDocument returned 'intact' with the forged block, which is what GET /runs/:id/rendered serves as {data, sealed:true}.
findings.failureScenario: Anyone holding app-role DB write access (the threat this change exists to detect: 'the app role writes report_snapshots') can do this in three writes. Targets are a never-finalized run or any final run sealed before the chain row existed. The run then reports 'intact' and displays fabricated content as the sealed record, with no signature. The detail text asserts a chain verification that never happens and that the integrity report would never perform for this row.
findings.suggestedFix: Also read sha256_chain, hmac_seal and chain_seq. Refuse a finalization row that is unchained (sha256_chain or chain_seq NULL). Where the audit HMAC key is configured, verify the row's hmac_seal, as verifyAuditChainSeals does for sealed rows. For a documentStored finalization, require the electronic_signatures row for report-run:<id>, and cross-check its manifest/bound payload (it carries act.sealHash) against the chain row's sealHash; a missing or disagreeing signature is a mismatch. Reword the audit-chain detail to say only what this read checked. Add a dbtest that inserts an unchained row and expects 'mismatch'.

findings.title: Legacy finalization (chain row without documentStored) whose seal was removed from its snapshot reads 'not-verifiable', not 'mismatch', contrary to the module's own contract
findings.evidence: Lines 179-182: `if (seal && !s.ok) return mismatch; if (sealedDocument) ...; return { verdict: 'not-verifiable', checks }`. With seal === null the first branch is skipped. Probe: verifyStoredSeal({seal:null, sealedDocument:null, chain:{...CHAIN, documentStored:false}, chainRows:1}) returned verdict 'not-verifiable'. Its checks were audit-chain ok, stored-seal 'No seal is stored with this run.', and stored-document 'No sealed document is stored'. The module header says: 'Only a run sealed before the document was stored, and whose stored seal agrees with what the chain recorded, is "not verifiable"'. A missing seal does not agree. The finalize code that wrote those chain rows (7d0d21e2) stored the seal whenever a snapshot existed, and POST /runs always creates one. readSealedDocument (line 186) collapses 'no snapshot row' and 'snapshot without seal' into the same nulls, so the read cannot tell the two apart.
findings.failureScenario: Take a run finalized between 7d0d21e2 and this change, where the chain row records a seal hash. If someone deletes `seal` from its snapshot_metadata, GET /runs/:id/seal answers 'not-verifiable' (looks like a legacy limitation) instead of 'mismatch' (a removal).
findings.suggestedFix: Have readSealedDocument report whether the latest snapshot row exists. For a chain row without documentStored, treat 'snapshot exists but no seal' as a mismatch. Keep 'not-verifiable' only for 'no snapshot at all' and for 'seal present and agrees, no document'. Add the missing unit case.

findings.title: Verification crashes (500) on a malformed stored document whenever the chain check fails, instead of returning the 'mismatch' verdict / 409
findings.evidence: Line 165: `documentCheck(sealedDocument, seal, c.ok ? chain : null)`. When the chain check fails (0 rows, 2+ rows, or payload unbound), recordedSeal (line 133) falls back to the mutable stored seal. A seal written beside the malformed document matches it, so extractProvenanceAtoms (seal.ts) runs on it unguarded. Probes: sections [{blocks:null}] gives "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'forEach')"; sections [null] gives "(reading 'blocks')"; provenance [null] gives "(reading 'sourceTable')". readRunSeal and readVerifiedSealedDocument both throw over a client returning snapshot {seal:{...contentHash: computeContentHash(bad)}, sealedDocument: bad} with no chain rows. readSealedDocument only checks Array.isArray(sections).
findings.failureScenario: A tampered snapshot on a run with no (or duplicate) finalization rows makes GET /runs/:id/seal answer 500 'reading seal' and GET /runs/:id/rendered answer 500. The verdict computed just before is 'mismatch' / 409 SEALED_DOCUMENT_MISMATCH. The module promises 'an error is never a verdict', but here the verification itself crashes on a malformed row.
findings.suggestedFix: Compute the document check only against the chain's record (skip it, or mark it not run, when c.ok is false), or validate the document's shape (sections[].blocks arrays of objects, provenance arrays of objects) before extracting atoms. Treat a malformed document as a failed stored-document check.

findings.title: Check details contradict each other when the chain check fails: the document 'hashes to the recorded seal' against an unrecorded seal; 'no recorded finalization' when there are two
findings.evidence: Probe, chainRows=0 with doc and seal: verdict mismatch, but the checks are [audit-chain false 'The audit chain holds no finalization of this run.', stored-seal false 'There is no recorded finalization to check the stored seal against.', stored-document **true** 'The stored document hashes to the recorded seal, and its provenance atoms match.'] (line 152). The 'recorded seal' here is the mutable snapshot copy (recordedSeal fallback, line 133). With chainRows=2 the stored-seal detail (line 120) still says 'There is no recorded finalization' although the first check says '2 finalizations'. The same happens when a row exists but is payload-unbound. The 409 message on GET /rendered (report-os.ts:1886) says the record 'no longer matches its finalization on the audit chain' even when the chain holds no finalization.
findings.failureScenario: A reviewer reading GET /runs/:id/seal on a tampered run sees a passing 'stored-document' check claiming agreement with 'the recorded seal' and a statement that no finalization is recorded, both false for that state. This is misleading in a Part 11 verification view.
findings.suggestedFix: When the chain check fails, report the document check as not performed, or say explicitly that it was compared with the stored, unrecorded seal. Make the stored-seal detail distinguish 'none recorded', 'recorded more than once' and 'recorded row unbound'. Give the 409 a message that does not presuppose a chain finalization.

findings.title: Run status is read outside the tenant transaction that reads the chain, so a concurrent finalize yields a transient false 'mismatch' / 409 SEALED_DOCUMENT_MISMATCH
findings.evidence: GET /runs/:id/seal reads report_runs.status via `db` at line 1917, then opens a separate inTenantTransaction (line 1923) that reads audit_logs. GET /rendered does the same: line 1862, then the registry read, then line 1879. readRunSeal and readVerifiedSealedDocument then treat status!=='final' plus any chain row as a mismatch ('The audit chain records this run as finalized, but the run is now marked "completed"'; finalizedButNotFinal, run-seal.ts:252). The unit test "is a mismatch when the run's status was rewritten..." pins that mapping, for exactly the inputs a race produces. Under READ COMMITTED, separate statements also do not share a snapshot.
findings.failureScenario: User A finalizes a run. User B's GET /runs/:id/seal or /rendered read the status as 'completed' just before A's commit and the audit_logs row just after it. B receives verdict 'mismatch' or 409 'stored record no longer matches its finalization' for a run that was legitimately sealed a moment earlier.
findings.suggestedFix: Read the run status in the same statement as the chain rows, or in the same REPEATABLE READ transaction. Alternatively, re-read the status inside the tenant transaction after reading the chain rows, and treat 'chain row present' plus 'status now final' as the final path.

reasoning:
Confirmed against the working tree. The change is now committed at HEAD as 82450092, and run-seal.ts is unchanged from what was described.

1. The code does what the finding says. In verifyStoredSeal (server/services/report-os/sealing/run-seal.ts:175-182), take a chain row whose documentStored is false and where seal === null. The check `if (seal && !s.ok)` is skipped, then `if (sealedDocument)` is skipped, and the function returns 'not-verifiable'. I ran a temporary vitest probe and deleted it afterwards; the tree is clean. `verifyStoredSeal({seal:null, sealedDocument:null, chain:{...documentStored:false, sealHash:<hash>}, chainRows:1})` returned 'not-verifiable'. The audit-chain check was ok, stored-seal was not ok ("No seal is stored with this run."), and stored-document was not ok. Through readRunSeal, with a fake client returning a snapshot without `seal` plus a legacy chain row, the result was also 'not-verifiable'.

2. This contradicts the module's own contract. The header (lines 26-28) says: "Only a run sealed before the document was stored, and whose stored seal agrees with what the chain recorded, is 'not verifiable'". The test header (line 16) says the same: "only a seal from before the document was stored is 'not verifiable'". A missing seal does not agree with anything. No existing unit test covers seal:null together with documentStored:false.

3. The removal is a real signal. Legacy finalize in 7d0d21e2 (finalizeOnChain/writeFinalize) wrote the chain row (with sealHash) in the same transaction as the seal. It always stored the seal when a latest snapshot existed. Only POST /runs (report-os.ts ~1618) inserts snapshots, with isLatest:true, and nothing else creates or flips latest snapshots. So "snapshot exists, chain row exists, seal missing" can only mean the seal was removed afterwards. "No snapshot at all" is a legitimate legacy case, because the run and snapshot inserts are not transactional. readSealedDocument returns only {seal, sealedDocument}, so it cannot tell these two cases apart.

Why the severity is low:
- Only legacy chain rows are affected. Those were written between 7d0d21e2 (02:10) and 82450092 (14:25) on 2026-10-01, roughly 12 hours.
- Removing the seal changes nothing observable except the check detail. An untampered legacy run (seal agrees, no document) is also 'not-verifiable', which I confirmed in the probe. So GET /rendered behaves identically: it re-renders from live data in both cases and never returns 409. GET /seal returns the seal as the chain recorded it in both cases. The stored-seal check already reports "No seal is stored with this run."
- Deleting the whole snapshot row would still read as 'not-verifiable' even after the suggested fix.

So the defect is a mislabelled verdict that breaks the documented contract, not a path that hides tampering in a way the current behavior would otherwise expose.

I reproduced the finding on the current working tree. The change is already committed as 82450092, so I read run-seal.ts from HEAD. I then ran scratchpad/probe-forge.ts against the running local database concept2cure-ri_dbtest. The probe acts as app_service, with is_superuser off, app.rls_enforce=on and the tenant set, and it runs in one transaction that is rolled back.

It made three app-role writes:
1. It set report_runs.status to 'final' on a run that was never finalized.
2. It wrote a forged {seal, sealedDocument} into report_snapshots.
3. It inserted one audit_logs row: action report_os.run_finalized, documentStored:true, payload_hash = sha256(new_values), and sha256_chain left NULL.

Results:
- readRunSeal returned verdict 'intact' with signature null, and all three checks were ok.
- The audit-chain detail said "the chain link itself is verified by the audit-trail integrity report".
- readVerifiedSealedDocument returned 'intact' with the block "FORGED: ready to file.". GET /rendered serves exactly that as {data, sealed:true}.
- The row read back as {sha256_chain:null, hmac_seal:null, chain_seq:null}.

Each supporting claim holds in code:
- readChainRecords (run-seal.ts:206-212) selects only new_values::text, payload_hash and occurred_at. The only binding it checks is payload_hash = sha256(nv), which any writer of the row can compute.
- The trigger audit_logs_chain_position (migrations/20260921_audit_logs_chain_seq.sql:100) returns NEW unchanged when sha256_chain IS NULL.
- sha256_chain is nullable, with no NOT NULL or CHECK constraint.
- readChainRows (chain.ts:650) reads only WHERE sha256_chain IS NOT NULL, so the integrity report never sees such a row. The detail text therefore claims a verification that never happens.
- verifyStoredSeal never requires the electronic_signatures row that finalize always writes in the same transaction. readRunSeal reads that row only for display.

What it does not affect:
- A run that already has a finalization row cannot be forged this way: a second row gives rows > 1, which is a mismatch.
- A stored document cannot be swapped under an existing chain hash.
- So the targets are runs that were never finalized, and final runs that have no chain row.

Why high and not lower:
- The attack needs app-role database write access. That is exactly the adversary the module names: its own comment says the snapshot is mutable because the app role writes it, and it treats the chain row as the trusted record.
- The result is fabricated content presented as the sealed Part 11 record, with no signature.

Caveats on the suggested fix:
- Requiring a non-NULL sha256_chain is not enough on its own. The app role can compute a valid sha256 link itself: the head is readable, and it can take the advisory lock and set the GUC.
- verifyAuditChainSeals skips rows whose hmac_seal is NULL.
- The e-signature signature_hash is a plain sha256 manifest hash.
- So only HMAC verification (when AUDIT_HMAC_KEY is set), plus requiring the signature and cross-checking its sealHash, materially raises the bar.
- None of this refutes the defect as reported.

The finding holds against the current tree. The change is now committed as 82450092, and run-seal.ts in the working tree matches what the finding describes.

The code path:
- verifyStoredSeal (run-seal.ts:165) calls `documentCheck(sealedDocument, seal, c.ok ? chain : null)`.
- When the chain check fails, `recordedSeal` (line 133) falls back to the mutable stored seal.
- If that seal's hash matches the stored document, line 147 calls `extractProvenanceAtoms(doc)` with no guard.
- In seal.ts:86-103, `extractProvenanceAtoms` dereferences `section.blocks.forEach` and `ref.sourceTable` directly.
- readSealedDocument (line 201) only checks `Array.isArray(sections)`.

I ran a tsx probe with a stub client. The snapshot held a malformed document plus a seal whose contentHash is `computeContentHash(bad, 2)`:
- Three malformed shapes: sections [{blocks:null}], sections [null], and a block with provenance [null].
- Three chain states where the check fails: zero rows, two rows, and one row whose payload_hash does not match.
- In all nine combinations, readRunSeal and readVerifiedSealedDocument both threw TypeErrors. The messages were exactly the ones the finding quotes: "reading 'forEach'", "reading 'blocks'" and "reading 'sourceTable'".
- With a single bound chain row, the same documents returned 'mismatch' and did not throw, because the hash check against the chain's sealHash fails before atoms are extracted.

Without the crash, all three failing-chain cases would return 'mismatch'. Zero rows with a document present is mismatch (line 172), and `!c.ok` is mismatch (line 174). So the document check cannot change the verdict there, yet it throws. Both routes catch the error and call serverError, which answers 500, instead of the 409 SEALED_DOCUMENT_MISMATCH or the mismatch view.

Why severity is low:
- Reaching this takes deliberate tampering with report_snapshots: a malformed document plus a matching seal, on a run with no, duplicate or unbound finalization rows. finalize already wrote report_os.run_finalized before this change, so legitimate zero-row runs are rare legacy cases.
- It fails closed. The document is never served as sealed; the only loss is the diagnostic verdict, since GET /seal cannot say which check failed.
- It does contradict the module's stated intent that an error is never a verdict: here verification itself crashes on bad data, not a failed read.

I ran verifyStoredSeal from server/services/report-os/sealing/run-seal.ts in the current working tree (the change is now commit 82450092) using npx tsx. Every case gives the right verdict, mismatch. The check details are what contradict each other.

- **chainRows=0, with a document and a seal:** audit-chain is false with "The audit chain holds no finalization of this run." stored-seal is false with "There is no recorded finalization to check the stored seal against." stored-document is TRUE with "The stored document hashes to the recorded seal, and its provenance atoms match." When the chain check fails, verifyStoredSeal passes chain=null (line 165). recordedSeal (lines 133-136) then falls back to the snapshot's own seal. So the "recorded seal" in that detail is the mutable stored copy, not anything the chain recorded.
- **chainRows=2:** audit-chain says "holds 2 finalizations". stored-seal still says "There is no recorded finalization..." (line 120), which is false. stored-document passes, again checked against the stored seal.
- **One row with payloadBound=false:** the same contradiction. stored-seal claims no finalization is recorded, and stored-document passes against the stored seal.

The module header says "The chain row is the record of the act", and elsewhere the file uses "recorded" for what the chain holds. The stored-document detail uses the same word for an unverified snapshot copy. That misleads in a Part 11 verification view.

The 409 at server/routes/report-os.ts:1886 says the stored record "no longer matches its finalization on the audit chain". That message is also returned when chainRows=0 and a document is stored, where the chain holds no finalization. That part is minor.

Severity is low because only the explanatory text is wrong. Every verdict is mismatch, and GET /rendered still refuses the document. No tampered record is shown as intact.

The finding holds against the current tree. The change has since been committed as 82450092, and the working-tree diff is empty.

Write side: finalizeOnChain → signGovernedAct (server/services/part11/governed-signature-ceremony.ts) runs four writes on one pooled client in one BEGIN…COMMIT. Those writes are the status UPDATE to 'final', the snapshot_metadata update and the 'report_os.run_finalized' chain row (in writeFinalize and writeReportEvent), plus the signature row. They become visible together at COMMIT.

Read side:
- GET /runs/:id/seal (report-os.ts ~1917) reads report_runs.status through `db`. That is a separate autocommit statement on another pool connection.
- Only afterwards does it open inTenantTransaction (a fresh connection, plain BEGIN, so READ COMMITTED; no REPEATABLE READ appears in this path) and call readRunSeal. That function reads audit_logs in a new statement with a new snapshot.
- GET /runs/:id/rendered does the same: status at ~1862, then the registry read, then inTenantTransaction at 1879 calling readVerifiedSealedDocument.

If A's finalize commits between B's status read and B's audit_logs read, B holds status 'completed' and also sees the chain row. finalizedButNotFinal (run-seal.ts:252) then returns the contradiction check. readRunSeal reports verdict 'mismatch' with "records this run as finalized, but the run is now marked "completed"". The /rendered route answers 409 SEALED_DOCUMENT_MISMATCH ("stored record no longer matches its finalization"). The unit tests at run-seal.test.ts:220 and :260 pin exactly that mapping for those inputs.

The opposite order cannot race. Seeing status 'final' implies the commit is visible, so the later chain and snapshot reads see it too.

Why low severity:
- The window is only the gap between two queries.
- It is transient; a retry gives the correct answer.
- The finalizer's own follow-up requests happen after commit.
- No data is corrupted.

It still deserves fixing: in a Part 11 surface it shows a false tamper signal for a legitimately sealed run. The suggested fix closes it. Re-read the status inside the tenant transaction after the chain read, or read status and chain rows in one statement or one REPEATABLE READ snapshot.
